topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: delete op-simulate and op-run-block
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See §14 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md).

## Goal

Delete `op-chain-ops/cmd/op-simulate` and `op-chain-ops/cmd/op-run-block`.

## Rationale

Both are geth-bound block-replay debugging tools that drive a full go-ethereum EVM (`vm.NewEVM`, `core.ApplyTransaction`, `types.MakeSigner`) over an OP-loaded chain config — i.e. op-geth **as a library**. They are standalone `main` packages with **no Go importers** and no CI/justfile/script references (only a line in [op-chain-ops/README.md](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-chain-ops/README.md)). Removing them deletes a geth-as-library dependency the decoupling would otherwise have to carry to upstream go-ethereum.

If equivalent block-replay debugging is needed later, reimplement it in Rust against op-reth.

## Scope

- Delete `op-chain-ops/cmd/op-simulate/` and `op-chain-ops/cmd/op-run-block/`.
- Drop their entries from `op-chain-ops/README.md` and any build wiring.

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: remove op-program from the monorepo
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20266 → #20257. The plan (PR #19767) excludes op-program from the decoupling because it depends on op-geth state execution (`core/state`, `core/vm`). The in-tree replacement lives at [`rust/kona`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/develop/rust/kona) (client + host). This issue tracks op-program's actual removal from the monorepo — a prerequisite for the final `go.mod` cutover (#20266) since op-program shares the monorepo's single `go.mod`.

## Context

op-program has **no separate `go.mod`** — it's part of the root module, so it uses the same `replace github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum => ... op-geth` directive. As long as op-program is in the module, the cutover can't flip that directive.

## External consumers (need migration first)

In-scope packages currently import op-program Go packages:

**op-challenger (Go code):**
- `op-challenger/game/fault/trace/super/provider_supervisor.go`, `provider_supernode.go` → `op-program/client/interop/types`
- `op-challenger/game/fault/trace/cannon/provider.go` → `op-program/host/types`, `op-program/host/kvstore`
- `op-challenger/game/fault/trace/utils/preimage.go` → `op-program/client/l1`
- (plus test files referencing the same packages)

**op-devstack (runtime artefact references):**
- `op-devstack/sysgo/add_game_type.go`, `superroot.go` → `op-program/bin/prestate-*.json` paths
- `op-devstack/shared/challenger/challenger.go` → `op-program/bin/op-program` binary path (used as the Cannon fraud-proof server)

**Build configs:**
- `Makefile`, `justfile`, `.golangci.yaml` entries for op-program

## Scope

1. **Relocate the Go packages op-challenger depends on.** For each imported op-program subpackage, either move the relevant types to `op-core/` (if stable and reusable) or fold the minimal needed surface into op-challenger itself. Packages to handle:
   - `op-program/client/interop/types` — interop message types
   - `op-program/host/types` — KV store types
   - `op-program/host/kvstore` — KV store impl
   - `op-program/client/l1` — L1 preimage helpers
2. **Swap op-challenger imports** to the new locations; remove `op-program` from its import graph.
3. **Update op-devstack runtime references** to use `rust/kona` artifacts (kona-host binary + prestate files) instead of `op-program/bin/*`. Blocked on `rust/kona` reaching production-readiness for the Cannon fraud-proof server role. If not yet ready, leave a clear TODO rather than stale paths.
4. **Delete `op-program/`** from the repo.
5. **Remove op-program targets** from `Makefile`, `justfile`, `.golangci.yaml`, and any CI workflows.
6. **Confirm `go mod tidy`** cleanly drops op-program's transitive deps.

## Dependencies

- Unblocks #20266 (can't flip `go.mod` to upstream go-ethereum while op-program still imports op-geth).
- May be blocked on `rust/kona` reaching the point where devstack/op-challenger integration tests can run against kona-host instead of op-program (coordinate with the kona track in the monorepo).

## Out of scope

- Further `rust/kona` development beyond what's needed to replace op-program's roles.
- Rewriting op-challenger's fault-proof logic — only the imports/paths change, not the algorithms.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: create op-core/params (OptimismConfig, ChainConfig, LoadChainConfig)
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See plan §5, §6 in the op-geth decoupling doc (PR #19767).

## Goal

Create `op-core/params` containing OP-specific chain config types that wrap upstream `params.ChainConfig`. Consumers import as `opparams`.

## Scope

### `OptimismConfig` struct

Mirrors op-geth's `params.OptimismConfig` verbatim. JSON field names must be preserved for wire compatibility (`rollup.Config.ChainOpConfig` is serialised).

```go
type OptimismConfig struct {
    EIP1559Elasticity        uint64  `json:"eip1559Elasticity"`
    EIP1559Denominator       uint64  `json:"eip1559Denominator"`
    EIP1559DenominatorCanyon *uint64 `json:"eip1559DenominatorCanyon,omitempty"`
}
```

Keep the `Optimism` prefix (exception to the naming rule) — the field is `ChainConfig.Optimism *OptimismConfig` and the type pairs with the field name.

### `ChainConfig` struct

Embeds upstream `params.ChainConfig`, adds OP hardfork fields + methods:
- Fields: `Optimism *OptimismConfig`, `BedrockBlock *big.Int`, `RegolithTime`, `CanyonTime`, `EcotoneTime`, `FjordTime`, `GraniteTime`, `HoloceneTime`, `IsthmusTime`, `JovianTime`, `KarstTime`, `InteropTime` (all `*uint64`).
- Methods: `IsOptimism()`, `IsCanyon(t uint64)`, `IsEcotone(t)`, `IsFjord(t)`, `IsGranite(t)`, `IsHolocene(t)`, `IsIsthmus(t)`, `IsJovian(t)`, `IsKarst(t)`, `IsBedrock(num *big.Int)`, plus `IsOptimism*` convenience variants where used.

Mirror op-geth's semantics for each method.

### `LoadChainConfig`

Replaces op-geth's `params.LoadOPStackChainConfig`. Takes a `*superchain.ChainConfig` (from `op-core/superchain`) and returns `*opparams.ChainConfig` with all OP fields populated.

### Wire / migration details

- `rollup.Config.ChainOpConfig` changes type from `*params.OptimismConfig` to `*opparams.OptimismConfig` in a follow-up sub-issue — but only the type change; JSON output must be identical.
- No removal of upstream `params` imports — consumers use both `params` and `opparams` via import aliases.

## Dependencies

- Benefits from #20259 (`op-core/superchain`) being available for the `LoadChainConfig` input type, but can be worked on in parallel with placeholder types.

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topPRs.title: [codex] batcher consensus proof of concept
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This draft PR adds a blob-mode-only batcher consensus proof of concept.

- adds a rollup config verifier address and batcher proof endpoint wiring
- attaches proof calldata to blob batcher transactions without changing blob batch data
- verifies blob transaction calldata in op-node derivation via block-hash `eth_call` to an L1 verifier contract and skips invalid proofs
- adds verifier logs, metrics, and unit coverage for batcher, derivation, L1 client, and verifier helpers
- adds DevStack verifier and sidecar options, valid/invalid acceptance tests, OP Up demo mode, and `op-up smoke-batcher-consensus`
- adds a Rust proof sidecar that runs Commonware Simplex over a simulated 4-validator network and emits the resulting finalization certificate
- switches the Simplex certificate scheme to Commonware secp256r1 so the certificate signatures are EVM-checkable
- carries a `CWSIMPLX1 || digest || marker || fixed POC envelope || Commonware certificate` calldata envelope for the Commonware sidecar path
- verifies the Commonware Simplex finalization certificate in the DevStack L1 verifier by checking the proposal digest, signer bitmap, quorum signatures, and P256 signatures over `sha256(union_unique(finalize_namespace, proposal.encode()))`
- activates Osaka on the DevStack L1 preset used by the Commonware verifier so the L1 `eth_call` path has the P256 precompile available
- makes the OP Up batcher-consensus demo self-contained by using the no-fault-proofs single-chain preset and adding `--l2-rpc-port` for running valid and invalid demo networks side by side

## POC Caveat

The current sidecar runs a deterministic in-process Commonware Simplex network for the POC. The verifier now directly checks the Commonware secp256r1 certificate signatures in EVM, but the certificate layout and validator set are still fixed for this proof of concept rather than a production configurable committee/verifier contract.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path op-batcher-consensus-sidecar/Cargo.toml

go test ./op-service/batchconsensus ./op-devstack/sysgo -run 'TestBuild|TestBatchConsensusMockVerifier|TestBuildCommonware|TestBuildSigned' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusValidProofAdvancesSafeHead' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusInvalidProofDoesNotAdvanceSafeHead' -count=1 -v

go test ./op-up -run '^$'
go run ./op-up --help
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all --help

# live OP Up demo smoke, with one shell per long-running devnet:
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-valid --batcher-consensus-poc
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-invalid --batcher-consensus-poc --batcher-consensus-poc-invalid --l2-rpc-port 8546
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all

git diff --check
```

The DevStack acceptance tests show valid Commonware consensus proof calldata advancing `local-safe`, and invalid proof calldata being rejected with `false batch consensus verifier result` while `local-safe` remains at genesis.

The live OP Up smoke run started a valid proof demo on `http://localhost:8545` and an invalid proof demo on `http://localhost:8546`; `smoke-batcher-consensus all` observed the valid safe head reach the submitted transfer block and the invalid safe head stay below the submitted transfer block for 20 seconds.

Note: the DevStack and OP Up runs used `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` in this environment because op-reth was not built locally.

topPRs.title: op-up: add devstack preset devnet UX
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a friendlier `op-up` UX for launching local op-devstack devnet presets.

This lets users run preset devnets from `op-up`, get randomized local RPC ports automatically, and see the information needed to interact with the network after startup.

## Changes

- Add `op-up up <preset>` / preset selection UX backed by op-devstack presets.
- Print service endpoints for L1/L2 EL, L2 CL, L1 beacon, and interop supernode RPC when available.
- Print deployed L1 contract addresses for each L2, including portal, system config, bridge, DGF, proxy admin, and delayed WETH.
- Use random local ports by default so users do not need to manually pick ports.
- Export devnet config files under `~/.op-up/configs/`, including endpoints, contracts, rollup configs, dependency set config, and generated JSON configs when available.
- Improve devstack temp-dir prefixes so op-up service logs/config artifacts are easier to identify by preset and service name.

topPRs.title: op-up: add devnet preset runner and control CLI
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds a friendlier `op-up` UX for launching local op-devstack devnet presets.

This lets users run preset devnets from `op-up`, get randomized local RPC ports automatically, and see the information needed to interact with the network after startup.

## Features

- Start realistic OP Stack devnets with one command.
- Pick from useful presets like minimal, interop, two-L2, multinode, conductors, and flashblocks.
- No manual port management: op-up finds ports and prints every endpoint.
- Get the funded test account, deployed contracts, L1 beacon RPC, L2 RPCs, and supernode RPC in one place.
- Export configs automatically for external tools like challenger/proposer runners.
- Control running services with start, stop, restart, and status.
- Simulate failures without editing presets or writing custom test code.
- Keep RPC endpoints stable across service restarts.
- Find service logs easily under ~/.op-up/logs.

## Changes

- Add `op-up up <preset>` / preset selection UX backed by op-devstack presets.
- Print service endpoints for L1/L2 EL, L2 CL, L1 beacon, and interop supernode RPC when available.
- Print deployed L1 contract addresses for each L2, including portal, system config, bridge, DGF, proxy admin, and delayed WETH.
- Use random local ports by default so users do not need to manually pick ports.
- Export devnet config files under `~/.op-up/configs/`, including endpoints, contracts, rollup configs, dependency set config, and generated JSON configs when available.
